faq.privacyAnswer: OpenKrisp processes your audio locally on your device. It doesn’t upload audio to a cloud service for noise reduction. Your call app still handles the call itself.
faq.independentQuestion: Can I reduce noise on just one side of the call?
faq.independentAnswer: Yes. Noise reduction has separate controls for your microphone audio and the audio you hear. Turn it on for either or both.
faq.appsQuestion: Which call apps can I use it with?
faq.appsAnswer: Use a call app that lets you choose your microphone and speakers. Select OpenKrisp Microphone and OpenKrisp Speaker in its audio settings. Compatibility is still being tested during the beta.
faq.platformsQuestion: Is it available for Windows or Intel Macs?
faq.platformsAnswer: The current beta targets Apple Silicon Macs and x86-64 Linux. Windows and Intel Mac installers aren’t provided.
faq.musicQuestion: Can I use it for music or without headphones?
faq.musicAnswer: Noise reduction is designed for speech. Use your usual audio output for music. Start with headphones for calls; speakerphone use hasn’t been validated yet.
